messages:
incident-bot: Pager: severity=sev2 — multiple nodes NotReady in cluster-prod-us-east-1, target: inference-pool-2, affected pods: redwood-runtime

Alice M.: saw the page. checking k8s. quick status: ~5/20 nodes NotReady in inference-pool-2, pods evicting, a few container restarts. latency spike for hosted API in us-east.

Ben R.: copying. running: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=inference-pool-2 -o wide`
```
NAME                STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
ip-10-1-2-3         NotReady   <none>   24d   v1.26.3
ip-10-1-2-4         Ready      <none>   24d   v1.26.3
...
```

Carol S.: logs look like `kubelet` restarts + GPU driver warnings on the NotReady hosts. suspect intermittent driver crash -> node NotReady.

Alice M.: can you paste the kubelet journal snippet?

Carol S.: grabbing.
```
Mar 03 12:07:25 ip-10-1-2-3 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 03 12:07:25 ip-10-1-2-3 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
Mar 03 12:07:26 ip-10-1-2-3 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Unit entered failed state.
```

Ben R.: Xid 31 is a GPU driver hang. previous incidents showed driver v525.60.11 has a known regression on that instance type. list kernel+driver versions?

Alice M.: nodes show nvidia-driver: 525.60.11 and kernel 5.15.0-101. also saw some OOMKills in container logs for runtime-proxy which might be cascading.

ops-runner-bot: auto-mitigation suggestion: cordon NotReady nodes, scale up inference-pool-2 on replacement-capacity group, route traffic to inference-pool-1 as fallback. See runbook: https://runbook.internal/infra/node-flap

Elaine (oncall): I'm oncall, taking lead. immediate actions: 1) cordon NotReady nodes to avoid new pods scheduling 2) scale up replacement nodes 3) trigger model fallback routing for critical customers. Ben/Carol, can you run cordon/drain and open a ticket to infra to roll GPU driver?

Ben R.: ack. cordoning the NotReady nodes now.
```bash
kubectl cordon ip-10-1-2-3
kubectl drain ip-10-1-2-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

Carol S.: creating infra ticket: INFRA-1342 with logs and suggested driver roll back to 520.x. pinging infra slack channel.

Alice M.: scaling replacement pool: `kops/terraform apply` not ideal during incident, using autoscaling group warmup: setting desired capacity +3 for replacement-capacity group.

ops-runner-bot: scaling event started for asg/replacement-capacity (+3). Estimated 2m to join cluster.

Elaine (oncall): routing control: enabling fallback route for high-priority tenants to inference-pool-1. This avoids model-quality changes because pools run same model version. Doing gradual traffic shift.

Alice M.: started reroute: `POST /admin/route` -> switched 15% traffic, monitoring errors.

Ben R.: observed model runtime crash metrics drop as traffic shifts. however latency still elevated for some requests that hit retry paths.

Carol S.: reviewing dmesg on affected host, also saw repeated GPU resets prior to kubelet crash. paste: `NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus` and `nvidia: GPU detached` 

Elaine (oncall): customer impact: initial spike caused ~4-6% 5xxs for us-east, top affected customers: 9 tenants with degraded latency (SLAs at risk). Notifying CS on current mitigation + ETA for roll back.

Alice M.: temporary mitigation successful: currently 70% of production traffic routed to healthy pools, errors down to ~1.5%. still seeing 1-2 nodes flip NotReady intermittently.

Ben R.: infra responded, they can roll driver in a staged fashion. plan: roll to 520.78.02 on a small subset, observe 30m, then full roll.

ops-runner-bot: automated diagnostics uploaded: /artifacts/incidents/1769876543/nvidia-diagnostics.tar.gz

Carol S.: found a container OOM pattern on runtime-proxy when the node partially lost GPU; OOM happened during fallback to CPU code path. Might need memory limit bump or smoother fallback. Filing a follow-up: RUNTIME-789.

Elaine (oncall): summary so far for handoff: root cause = GPU driver hangs (Xid 31) -> kubelet restarts -> node NotReady -> evictions -> latency/5xxs. Mitigations applied: cordon/drain, scale replacement nodes, routed traffic to inference-pool-1, infra driver rollback planned. Current status: errors reduced, still active.

Alice M.: timeline note: incident opened 12:06, initial mitigation by 12:14, traffic reroute 12:22, replacement nodes joining 12:28.

Ben R.: ops -> infra will start staged roll at 12:45. expected impact minimal.

Elaine (oncall): I'm handing off to Ben for the next 2 hours while I go offline. Ben, please continue runbook steps, keep CS updated, and escalate if errors creep above 3%. I'll be reachable by DM for urgent questions.

Ben R.: taking over. I'll update thread with any roll progress or regression. I've added a short incident note: `/incident create node-flap-inference-1769876543`

Carol S.: recommend follow-ups after the incident: 1) pin working driver or add automated rollback, 2) add kubelet restart alert suppression window to avoid cascading evictions, 3) adjust runtime-proxy memory limits for graceful CPU fallback.

ops-runner-bot: incident status changed -> active -> mitigated=false -> owner=Ben R.

Ben R.: copy. continuing monitoring, will update when driver roll completes or if errors increase. :thumbsup:

Elaine (oncall): handing summary sent to #customer-updates for CS draft. Good job team.
